Realistic NIAH · non-thinking · V4.1–V4.4

Where does the running count live—and what does generation use?

A v10-style representation analysis plus held-out causal tests. The report separates span_end from span_mean, fits representation geometry and intervention targets on discovery seeds only, and tests broad-head necessity, exact needle-end transport, exact answer-query state transport, and answer-query geometric steering on confirmation seeds.

Controlled relaxation ladder

The unit of representation analysis is one N=10 prompt. Its ten occurrence vectors are ordered by the nested needle index. Discovery uses seeds 1234–1253; confirmation uses 1254–1263. Final-output labels always come from actual greedy generation, never candidate probability.

V4.1all fixed

Position, city-score order, and city-score content fixed across seeds.

V4.2position released

Needle positions vary; order and semantic content remain fixed.

V4.3order released

Positions and city-score order vary; content remains fixed.

V4.4content released

Position, order, and city-score content all vary across seeds.

Interpretation rule. A clean v4.1 curve can be an identity/order/position code. Evidence for a content-independent counter requires geometry and count decoding to persist into v4.3 and especially v4.4.

Primary-layer confirmation metrics

Each pooling’s layer is selected once, using maximum grouped-seed ridge cross-validation R² on v4.1 discovery only. No confirmation label enters layer selection. Lower MAE and noise/signal are better; higher R², linear CKA, and distance correlation are better.

This is the requested switchable 3D counter view. Drag to rotate, use the mouse wheel to zoom, and switch any displayed axis among PC1–PC6. Span-end attention–undercount alignment

This analysis is intentionally restricted to span_end. It asks whether the answer-query attention ensemble assigns unusually low mass to the evidence implied by an undercount. All estimates use confirmation seeds only; head ranking is frozen from discovery data within each model × variant, and the top eight discovery-ranked broad heads are averaged after each head is normalized to mean occurrence share 1.

Behavior labelActual greedy integer output N̂; no sequence probability or candidate score enters the label. Unparseable and non-undercount outputs are outside this estimand.
Held-out unitTen confirmation seeds (1254–1263); prompts within a seed remain in the same resampling cluster.
Uncertainty20,000 percentile bootstrap resamples of seed-level means.
TestingTwo-sided exact seed sign-flip tests under the symmetry null; Holm families are the two pooled model tests and, separately, the eight variant panels.

1. Behavior-implied omitted tail versus the lowest-attention occurrences

For a gold count N and an undercount N̂, let k = N − N̂. The behavior-implied omitted tail is Tk = {N−k+1,…,N}; the attention-implied candidate set Bk contains the k occurrence endpoints with the lowest ensemble attention. The primary score is their overlap fraction.

S = |Bk ∩ Tk| / k. If Bk were a uniformly random k-subset, E[S] = k/N and P(Bk = Tk) = 1 / C(N,k).

The estimand is the seed-equal mean of S − k/N. To avoid selecting the most favorable relaxation, the cross-variant aggregate gives each variant equal weight inside each seed; the variant panels expose heterogeneity. This analysis was not preregistered, so its intervals and tests are inferential audits rather than confirmatory claims. “Exact / random” reports the observed exact-set-match rate and its combinatorial chance baseline. Tail/prefix is the mean normalized attention on the behavior-implied tail divided by the retained prefix; values below 1 indicate suppressed tail attention.

2. Exact newly added needle in nested N−1 → N pairs

The tail analysis identifies an omitted set only under an ordering assumption. The nested design supplies a sharper check: the newly introduced Nth occurrence is known exactly. We retain transitions ending in an undercount for both groups, then compare (i) whether that new endpoint falls inside the current bottom-k attention set and (ii) its normalized attention share, where 1 is uniform over occurrences. “Failed” means the greedy output did not increase; “registered” means it increased by exactly one. Statuses are first matched within seed × variant; matched variant contrasts are then averaged inside seed. Holm correction is applied across the two models separately for each nested estimand.

Qwen3-8B tail alignment.

The equal-variant pooled contrast is +0.197 [0.105, 0.286], Holm p=0.016. All four variant point estimates are above chance. The 95% seed-cluster interval excludes zero for v4.1, v4.2, v4.3, and v4.4; the exact sign-flip test remains below 0.05 after Holm correction for v4.1.

Gemma4-E4B tail alignment.

The equal-variant pooled contrast is +0.127 [0.045, 0.221], Holm p=0.016. All four variant point estimates are above chance. The 95% seed-cluster interval excludes zero for v4.1, and v4.4; the exact sign-flip test remains below 0.05 after Holm correction for v4.1.

Exact new-needle check.

Qwen3-8B: risk difference +0.158 [-0.001, 0.309], Holm p=0.141; Gemma4-E4B: risk difference +0.170 [0.015, 0.321], Holm p=0.141. Positive values mean the newly added needle is more often in the bottom-k attention set when the output fails to increment.

Inference boundary. The tail set is behavior-implied, not an observed record of which occurrences the model “forgot.” The nested increment diagnostic identifies the added occurrence exactly, but attention remains correlational. These results motivate—and do not replace—the registered ablation and endpoint residual-patching tests.

Severe class imbalance. Qwen has no correct N=10 confirmation trajectory in any variant; Gemma has one in v4.1 and none in v4.2–v4.4. Therefore the correct/wrong switch is an audit view, not a powered group comparison. The causal studies should stratify by the baseline outcome over the full count grid, where both correct and wrong examples are available.

Causal screen: necessity, transport, and manipulability

The completed screen_8h_v1 and answer_query_dense_v1 campaigns keep all four variants and all ten confirmation seeds while narrowing interventions to the most diagnostic conditions. Every row is scored from the complete deterministic greedy continuation after Total:; candidate probabilities never define correctness or effect size.

Head necessityDiscovery-ranked span_end top-4/top-8 heads are ablated only at the answer-query row for counts 7–10, with one layer-matched random set.
Endpoint transportThe exact toggled needle-end residual is copied from donor to receiver cumulatively from three matched depths for 5↔6, 7↔8, and 9↔10.
Exact query transportThe single residual state at the prompt-final Total: query is copied at eight separate layers for 5↔6, 7↔8, 9↔10, and 5↔10. The donor is another real prompt; no span mean or output-token state is used.
Query manipulabilityDiscovery-fit count-centroid deltas steer the answer-query residual for 7↔8, 9↔10, and 5↔10, with an orthogonal norm-matched random vector.
Inference unitPoint estimates weight prompts equally; intervals resample ten paired seeds after averaging variants and count pairs within seed. Primary sign-flip tests use ten seeds and Holm correction within each intervention family.
Qwen3-8B broad-head necessity.

Top-8 ranked ablation changes 23.1% of outputs versus 10.0% for layer-matched random heads. The paired count-shift contrast is -0.331 [-0.412, -0.256], Holm p=0.008. Negative means stronger undercount after ablating ranked heads.

Gemma4-E4B broad-head necessity.

Top-8 ranked ablation changes 97.5% of outputs versus 45.0% for layer-matched random heads. The paired count-shift contrast is -2.156 [-2.356, -1.969], Holm p=0.008. Negative means stronger undercount after ablating ranked heads.

Transport/manipulability dissociation.

Qwen3-8B L26: aligned geometric-minus-random shift +0.958 [+0.808, +1.096], Holm p=0.012; Gemma4-E4B L31: aligned geometric-minus-random shift +1.387 [+1.283, +1.488], Holm p=0.012. In contrast, exact needle-end residual patching moves toward the donor gold on at most 2.1% of rows at any tested layer. The answer-query count geometry is causally manipulable late, but the tested single endpoint is not a sufficient transport channel.

Exact query-state transport.

The first significant ≥50% donor-prediction adoption occurs at Qwen3-8B L26: 59.2% [52.0, 66.1]; Gemma4-E4B L31: 86.5% [82.8, 90.0]. At the final block the conservative eligible-row adoption rates are Qwen3-8B L35: 100.00%; Gemma4-E4B L41: 99.58%. Thus late answer-query state is a highly sufficient carrier of the model's already-computed prediction, sharply contrasting with the null needle-end transplant.

1. Discovery-ranked broad-head ablation

The primary contrast is ranked minus layer-matched random. A negative count-shift contrast means that removing the ranked heads produces a larger undercount than removing equally many control heads at the same layers. The table pools baseline-correct and baseline-wrong prompts because the high-count correct stratum is sparse; the saved summary and control tables retain the outcome strata.

This establishes a causal contribution of the selected bank, but it does not imply that every ranked head is individually broad or that the circuit computes an exact arithmetic sum.

2. Exact needle-end residual patching

This is the user-selected span_end intervention—not a span mean. A positive direction-aligned shift means insertion patches increase the output and removal patches decrease it. Moved requires a strict reduction in distance to the donor gold, so a receiver already equal to the donor gold does not count as transport.

Interpretation. The tested endpoint state is not a sufficient count-transport channel. This null does not erase the span-end decoding result: decodability, causal necessity, and cross-prompt transport are different properties. Position-specific routing, multiple needle tokens, or a distributed state may still be required.

3. Exact answer-query residual patching

This follow-up isolates the prompt-final Total: query state. Each row copies one donor residual vector into the receiver at exactly one layer, then performs complete greedy generation. The primary mechanistic estimand is adoption of the donor model prediction among rows where receiver and donor baseline predictions differ. It is deliberately distinct from donor-gold accuracy: a perfect transport can faithfully copy a donor that was itself wrong.

The receiver baseline is 5<turn|> with token IDs [236810, 106]; the donor baseline is 10<turn|> with IDs [236770, 236771, 106]; the patch emits 11<turn|> with IDs [236770, 236770, 106]. This is evidence for prefix transport followed by an unpatched autoregressive continuation error: the answer-query state supplies the first digit, whereas the next generated step is outside the single-position patch. Invalid eligible rows are counted as donor-adoption failures, never dropped from the primary rate.
Interpretation. Transport switches on abruptly between Qwen L18 and L26 and between Gemma L20 and L31. At the final layer, every valid eligible row follows the donor prediction; the conservative rate is 100% for Qwen and 99.58% for Gemma because Gemma's five strict-invalid 11 continuations count as failures. This establishes sufficiency of the late query state for the computed prediction, not that the state is a clean scalar counter or that the donor prediction is correct.

4. Answer-query geometric steering

At α=1, the applied vector is the discovery centroid difference from the receiver count to the target count. The primary effect is the generated-count shift aligned with the intended direction, paired against an orthogonal vector with the same norm. Moved and target hit use the intended count path, not token probability.

What this report can and cannot establish

Representation ≠ mechanism.

PCA, ridge decoding, and centroid geometry show availability of count-related information. They do not show that generation reads or needs it.

Span-end vs span-mean.

Span-end asks whether a localized terminal state carries the running index. Span-mean asks whether information is distributed across the full semantic needle span. Their PCA bases and primary layers are intentionally separate.

Screen, not full sweep.

The causal result covers top-4/top-8 span-end heads, exact toggled needle ends, exact answer-query states at eight layers, selected count pairs, α=1 centroid deltas, and one matched random control. It does not replace the larger registered grid.
